rename.to: beta.1 ngModel/ngModelChange not working in FireFox 43.0.4

body:
Also in Firefox 45.0a2 (2016-01-22).

Could be b44d36cf955acd81a3e7285ab0e1acbffe8c8dcc. It removes a `(change)` binding from `select` so as not to call onChange twice, but maybe in Firefox that `(change)` was needed?

Confirmed, I re-added the missing line and my selects work again.

I'm not going to submit a PR because it would break #5969. @vsavkin, any thoughts?

For 44.0 also doesn't work.

Temporary I've fix it locally with:

```
<select [ngModel]="value" (change)="changeValue($event.target.value)">
```

Bug is actual for _select_.

issue.title: [Mobile Chrome] ngControl(select[multiple]): input event won't fire
issue.body:
Mobile Chrome wont fire input event when select [multiple] interacted with,  thus breaking ngControl.

A current workaround is to subscribe to nativeElement change event an call ngControl updateValue from there.

Its also possible to implement select[multiple] selectedOptions handling with this approach, while there's no builtin support.

issue.title: [(ngModel)] on select does not work in IE10, IE11
issue.body:
When using ngModel on a select element and setting the model to the desired initial value in the constructor or ngOnInit, the select value stays empty. In Firefox and Chrome this works fine but not in IE10/IE11.

See the example Plunker here: http://embed.plnkr.co/EKQcB2ZtnEetRrLYUq78/ (Note this does not work in IE but you can check out the code used in app.ts)

issue.title: ngFormControl on select not changing if steered by webdriverjs/protractor3
issue.body:
Hey,

after Upgrading my Application from Beta.0 to Beta.1, Beta.2 or Beta.3 my Protractor-Tests won't trigger any value-changes on select-Controls. This seems to be related to this change: https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/b44d36cf955acd81a3e7285ab0e1acbffe8c8dcc
There got the change-Event dropped, which seems to be vital to Protractor.
Using the Application on my own, the select control works as expected. Protractor runs under Chrome 47.

Any ideas on this?

body: Circling back around - I've confirmed that @DenisKolodin's workaround works. Thanks!
